note: Development calibration key. Same rivals shape as the sealed release keys: a list of {explanation, distinguishing_prediction}.

rivals.explanation: Cabinet sensor S-A reads high in the afternoon because radiant heat warms its rear-wall bracket, while the cabinet air stays at setpoint.
rivals.distinguishing_prediction: Moving S-A to shelf height removes the afternoon offset, and the offset follows the rear-wall temperature and not the air temperature.

rivals.explanation: The cabinet air really is warm in the afternoon and reference probe R-1 reads low because of a probe fault or its placement.
rivals.distinguishing_prediction: A second independently calibrated probe at shelf height also reads about 30 C in the afternoon, and R-1 fails a fresh bath check.

rivals.explanation: Sensor S-A has a temperature-dependent calibration or electrical drift in the sensor itself.
rivals.distinguishing_prediction: S-A reads offset in a reference bath at afternoon ambient temperature, and the offset stays when S-A is moved to shelf height.
